title: Adaptive probing & lightweight evals — scratchpad
body:
Quick context:
- Purpose: lightweight, cheap probes to detect when model behavior drifts for a given prefix/cache state and route to a higher-fidelity variant or warm a KV cache.
- Why now: observed a couple of customer incidents where short-context churn + cheap quantized variants produced hallucination spikes; want an inexpensive early-detection signal.

Notes to self / hypotheses:
- H1: Small probe prompts (20–40 tokens) can detect prefix-sensitive failure modes faster than full evals. Not necessarily class-level accuracy, but relative score degradation.
- H2: Probe-level delta on log-prob or surprisal is a useful signal; combine with a cheap reranker/embedding similarity test.
- H3: Augment with lightweight synthetic perturbations (drop tokens, paraphrase) to stress memory dependency.

Design ideas (sketchy):
1) Probe suite per route/model
   - 8–12 short probes per customer route derived from top prompt families (sampling from production prompts)
   - Keep probes < 50 tokens; include 2 that test long-range facts and 2 that test recent-session coherence.
2) Signal aggregation
   - Score each probe with: mean token log-prob (from served model), token-level surprisal variance, and embedding-sim cosine distance to safe-reference answer embedding.
   - Combine into a single probe score S in [0,1] using a simple weighted sum; thresholds tuned per route.
3) Actions on threshold
   - Soft fallback: push traffic to a higher-precision (fp16->bf16->int8) variant for next N minutes.
   - Hard fallback: pin to dedicated capacity / route to host region with known higher capacity.
   - Warm: trigger a KV-cache warming job for model variant (prefetch top-k cached prefixes).

Implementation notes / low-fi plan:
- Build a cheap probe runner as a sidecar microservice that:
  a) pulls last N prompts per route (sample) from anonymized logs (prod-sampling).
  b) runs probe suite against the current model variant (hosted) and against an internal 'gold' benchmark variant (e.g., fp16 baseline).
  c) computes deltas and posts metrics to Console/tracing.
- Runtime budget: aim for <0.5% extra token cost across routes; prefer sampling windows (run probes every 5–15 minutes per active route).

Evaluation plan (what success looks like):
- True positive rate: probes trigger fallback within 3 minutes of a documented degradation event in 80%+ of incidents in the test window.
- False positive rate: probes trigger fallback less than 5% of routine non-problem windows.
- Cost: additional token spend under 0.5% monthly.
- Latency/regression: fallbacks should not add more than 30ms median to p90 latency for short requests (route-level SLA).

Quick experiment matrix (small-scale):
- Dataset: 2000 sampled real prompts from three customer routes (anonymized) + 500 synthetic stress prompts.
- Models: quantized-lowbit variant (q4_0-like), fp16 baseline, distilled small model (for reranker).
- Probe sets: random-sample probes vs. curated prompts derived from production top-queries.
- Metrics: probe_score_delta, post-fallback error-rate, user-visible failure metric (e.g., hallucination flag from downstream eval).

Open questions / TODOs (priority order):
- [ ] How to get representative probe seeds without exposing PII? (anonymize + replace entities) — talk to privacy/compliance.
- [ ] Tuning: How to pick thresholds per-route automatically? Explore percentile-based dynamic thresholds vs. static.
- [ ] Integration with Console: want token-level cost delta + a probe timeline view. Who owns the Console hook? Ping: Omar.
- [ ] Can we reuse Optimize recommendations (quantization profiles) as fallback targets? Follow up with Product-Optimize team.
- [ ] Simulate: write a small simulator that replays sampled logs and inserts synthetic drift to measure TPR/FPR.

Quick sketch of probe scoring snippet (pseudo):
- for probe in probes:
    toks, logps = model.score(probe.prompt)
    mean_lp = mean(logps[-len(answer_tokens):])
    surprisal_var = var(logps)
    emb_sim = cos(encoder.embed(answer_text), reference_embed)
    probe_score = sigmoid(a*(mean_lp_diff) + b*(1-emb_sim) + c*surprisal_var)

Operational considerations:
- Data retention: only keep probe results + anonymized traces for 30 days by default.
- Alerts: route-level alert if probe_score > route_threshold for 2 consecutive probe windows.
- Cost monitoring: add a budget cap per route that can disable probes if spend exceeds x% of route monthly spend.

Conference/paper links I want to re-read (quick bookmarks):
- "On the Use of Probes for Model Behavior Monitoring" (workshop note, 2027) — checklist for probe design
- "Surprisal and Token-level Diagnostics" (arXiv, 2026)
- Distillation + reranker patterns — internal slides: github.com/redwood-inference/internal-distill-slides
- Practical KV-warmup heuristics — community blog by DeepServe (2028)

Meeting notes snippets (from sync 2029-04-12):
- Mika: leaning toward percentile-based thresholds, per-route baselines.
- Omar: concerned about explosion of probes for multi-tenant hosts; suggests adaptive sampling (fewer probes for low-traffic routes).
- Taylor (me): emphasize cheapness; aim to keep detection-local and avoid full-eval unless triggered.

Next steps (next week):
- Prototype probe runner (minimal) + run on 3 sample routes internally (Mika + me).
- Write simulation harness and run 5 drift scenarios.
- Draft Confluence page with design + expected Console hooks for review.

Notes-to-self: keep probes simple first. If initial signals look noisy, iterate on embedding reference sets and synthetic perturbations. Remember to log decisions (why thresholds chosen) for future audits.

-----
Scratchpad/brainstorm archive (random fragments):
- "warm-top-k-cache" workflow might be expensive; consider lazy-warm on first post-probe request.
- Could we use tiny policy network (few-layer MLP) taking probe features to predict fallback action? Lightweight and trainable online.
- Consider gating based on traffic tier (paid customers get stricter fallback, free-tier gets relaxed).
- Slack ping draft: "experiments: launching adaptive-probes POC on sandbox routes Thu 2029-04-18. Would appreciate quick eyeballs on probe set selection."

End of notes.
